title: Hyperbolic Hierarchical Alignment for Video-Based Visible-Infrared Person Re-Identification
claim: Euclidean aggregation crowds diverse per-frame cues into one collapsed blob; hyperbolic aggregation keeps them as separate branches around a shared prototype.
layout: 2 stacked panels: image strips on top, side-by-side Euclidean vs hyperbolic below
description: The top panel (a) shows two strips of five pedestrian frames each. The left strip is a visible tracklet with a cyan arrow, and the right strip is a dark infrared tracklet with an orange arrow. Colored labels above the frames name the cue types: Occlusion (yellow), Pose Variation (teal), Viewpoint (gray) and Motion Blur (pink). The bottom panel (b) has two halves on a pale blue background. On the left, a rounded Euclidean box shows four colored dot clusters, one per cue. Blue arrows push them into a tangled multicolor blob labeled 'Cue Crowding'. On the right, a Poincaré disc has a gold 'Identity Prototype' at its center. Curved, color-coded branches labeled Occlusion, Pose, Motion Blur and Viewpoint fan outward. They end in teal circles for visible frames and orange triangles for infrared frames. The eye goes first to the photos, then to the colorful disc.
caption: Tracklets in visible and infrared modalities exhibit diverse frame-wise cues (e.g., occlusion and pose variations), making spatio-temporal aggregation challenging. Euclidean aggregation entangles diverse cues, causing cue crowding and collapsed embeddings. Hyperbolic aggregation preserves cue-wise structure around an identity prototype for robust video-level representations.
abstract: Video-based visible-infrared person re-identification (VVI-ReID) aims to learn robust video-level representations under modality discrepancy. However, existing methods typically rely on Euclidean geometry, which is suboptimal for modeling the complex temporal dynamics within visible and infrared tracklets, as it inevitably distorts the intrinsic hierarchical structure inherent in diverse temporal variations (e.g., occlusion, pose). In this paper, we propose Hyperbolic Hierarchical Alignment (HHA), which unifies spatio-temporal modeling and cross-modality alignment on the Poincaré ball. HHA employs a Hyperbolic Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Aggregator (HHSA) to organize time-varying cues into low-distortion hierarchical representations via Hyperbolic Geometry Interaction (HGI) and Dual-Geometry Fusion (DGF). Furthermore, we introduce Geometry-Aware Modality Alignment (GMA), which integrates Hyperbolic Modality Alignment (HMA) to couple modality centroids for geometric consistency and Hyperbolic Prototype Alignment (HPA) to anchor both modalities to shared identity prototypes for robust discrimination. Experiments on HITSZ-VCM and BUPTCampus demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. The code will be available at https://github.com/Visuang/HHA.
